review_summary: The junior differential captures the major cardiometabolic issues but under‑estimates the likelihood of the three most relevant conditions (hypertension, early CKD, OSA) and omits mechanistic entities that explain the critical laboratory abnormalities. Probabilities need recalibration, and additional diagnoses (distal RTA, NSAID nephropathy, resistant hypertension) should be added. Overall reasoning quality is solid but requires refinement and more complete laboratory data.
